title: Hiring/admissions disclaimer is opt-in only and absent from default reports
claim: The only 'do not use for hiring' warning in the report is inside the verbose_caveats branch; the default report and --scores-only/--json outputs carry no use restriction, while the tool is intended for screening people.

evidence.excerpt: if verbose_caveats or format_flag == "--verbose-caveats":
"    • Do not use these estimates for hiring, clinical, or legal decisions."

impact_on_screened_person: A recruiter receiving the default or slim score output sees an IQ number with no warning and may reject a candidate on it.
fix: Make a prohibited/high-risk-use notice mandatory in every output format (including --scores-only and --json via a 'use_restriction' field) and require an explicit use_context acknowledgement; refuse or degrade when context is hiring/admission.

title: No consent or lawful-basis capture for processing a person's text (UU PDP)
claim: Nothing in the server or pipeline records data-subject consent, lawful basis, or purpose before analysing a person's writing; UU PDP No. 27/2022 requires explicit consent/lawful basis and purpose limitation, and inferred IQ/education is sensitive profiling.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no consent, subject_id, purpose or lawful_basis parameter on any tool_* function (e.g. tool_detect_language(text: str))
**Privacy.** Text submitted to the MCP server is processed locally.

impact_on_screened_person: A person's writing is scored and profiled without their knowledge or ability to refuse, with no lawful basis on record.
fix: Add docs/compliance/consent-and-lawful-basis.md with consent text (ID/EN), purpose statement and lawful-basis matrix, and require a consent_ref + purpose argument that the pipeline refuses to run without.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/compliance/consent-and-lawful-basis.md exists and names UU PDP 27/2022 consent, purpose limitation and withdrawal procedure

title: No audit trail of who scored whom, when, with which model/norm version
claim: Scoring is stateless: no record of request, operator, input hash, norm file version, code version or output is persisted, so a contested decision cannot be reconstructed or defended.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no logging, audit record or request id anywhere in server.py

impact_on_screened_person: A rejected applicant cannot obtain or contest the basis of the decision, and the operator cannot prove what was computed.
fix: Emit an append-only audit record (UTC timestamp, operator id, SHA-256 of input, tool versions, norms hash, outputs) for every pipeline run, stored without raw text.

title: No human-in-the-loop gate or automated-decision safeguard
claim: Outputs are final numeric verdicts with a classification label; there is no review-required state, no override/appeal field and no block on fully automated use. UU PDP and the EU AI Act (Annex III employment/education) require human oversight and a right to contest automated decisions.

evidence.excerpt: line(f"  Classification  : {iq_result['classification']}")
absence: no human_review, reviewer or appeal parameter or state

impact_on_screened_person: A low-band label such as 'Low' can drive an automated rejection with nobody accountable and no route to appeal.
fix: Add a mandatory 'decision_status: advisory_only / requires_human_review' field to all outputs, a reviewer sign-off record, and refuse outputs shaped as pass/fail thresholds.

title: No adverse-impact (EEOC four-fifths) or subgroup fairness monitoring
claim: No code or doc computes selection-rate ratios or score gaps across protected groups (language, gender, region, ethnicity, age); the four-fifths rule and EU AI Act bias testing are unaddressed although norms are English-derived.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no subgroup or adverse-impact test; only per-function unit tests
line("    • IQ/VFS norms are English-derived and only approximately adapted to")

impact_on_screened_person: Indonesian-language and regional-dialect applicants are systematically scored lower and screened out at a disproportionate rate, undetected.
fix: Write docs/compliance/adverse-impact-protocol.md defining protected groups, selection-rate ratio and four-fifths check, and add scripts/adverse_impact.py that runs on a labelled cohort and fails below 0.8.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/compliance/adverse-impact-protocol.md exists and specifies four-fifths ratio computation and remediation threshold

title: Education-level inference is protected-attribute-adjacent with no safeguard
claim: estimate_education_level infers formal schooling (S1/S2/S3) from text style and the report asserts 'Writing style consistent with X authorship', producing credentials-like claims about a person that may be wrong and discriminatory in admissions.

evidence.excerpt: line(f"  Writing style consistent with {edu_result['level_en']} authorship.")
absence: no source, validation or citation for fog/ari/lexical-density thresholds

impact_on_screened_person: Self-taught or non-native writers are labelled as lower-educated, creating a false credential record that can bar them.
fix: Remove the education-level claim from default output or gate behind explicit non-screening use; add provenance metadata to edu_norms.json and a warning that it is not a credential.

title: No data minimisation: reports quote the subject's own sentences verbatim
claim: The report embeds verbatim sentences (truncated at 100 chars) as evidence in every section, and the mental-age and age inputs are collected though not necessary for any screening decision; this violates data minimisation and spreads personal content into reports.

evidence.excerpt: line(f"    → {_trunc(ev['sentence'])}")
def tool_predict_mental_age(iq_estimate: float, chronological_age: int = 0) -> str:

impact_on_screened_person: Sensitive personal statements and age (a protected attribute) are reproduced in documents that circulate to recruiters.
fix: Add a redact_evidence option defaulting on (sentence index plus triggers only) and make chronological_age opt-in with documented purpose.

title: No retention, deletion or data-subject-rights process
claim: There is no retention schedule, deletion procedure or access/correction/objection process for scored text or reports; example/ outputs show reports are written to disk as plain Markdown.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no retention period, deletion, data-subject access/erasure or DPO contact documented
absence: no output-handling or purge logic

impact_on_screened_person: A screened person has no way to have their profile deleted or corrected, contrary to UU PDP data-subject rights.
fix: Create docs/compliance/retention-and-dsr.md with retention schedule, erasure/access procedure, response SLAs and a DPO contact, and a purge script for stored reports.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/compliance/retention-and-dsr.md exists and defines retention period, erasure and access request SLAs

title: Privacy claim is unverified and cross-border transfer is unaddressed
claim: README asserts local processing and that nothing leaves the machine, yet the semantic model is downloaded from an external host and the MCP tool is invoked by a hosted LLM agent, which transmits the candidate's text to a third-party model provider; no cross-border transfer analysis (UU PDP) exists.

evidence.excerpt: No data is sent to external services beyond the embedding model (downloaded locally on first use).
chronological_age: "integer — improves mental age precision"

impact_on_screened_person: Candidate writing and age are sent to foreign model providers without notice or a transfer mechanism.
fix: Correct the privacy statement, and write docs/compliance/data-flow-and-transfer.md mapping every data flow including the agent/LLM host, with transfer basis and DPIA reference.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/compliance/data-flow-and-transfer.md exists and lists every external recipient with transfer basis

title: No DPIA or EU AI Act high-risk conformity documentation
claim: Employment/education screening is high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III and automated profiling requires a DPIA under UU PDP; the repo contains no DPIA, risk-management file, technical documentation or conformity assessment.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no DPIA, AI Act classification, or risk-management documentation
absence: no docs/compliance directory

impact_on_screened_person: Deploying without these exposes screened persons to an unassessed high-risk system and the operator to regulatory sanction.
fix: Produce docs/compliance/dpia.md and docs/compliance/ai-act-classification.md covering risk, mitigation, accuracy, oversight and logging.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/compliance/dpia.md exists and includes risk register, mitigations and sign-off section

title: Model and norm changes are uncontrolled and unversioned
claim: Norm files are loaded without version, hash or changelog and outputs omit any model_version, so a threshold edit silently changes every person's band; golden tests only pin outputs, not governance.

evidence.excerpt: _iq_norms = json.load(f)
"default_chronological_age": 30

impact_on_screened_person: Two applicants scored before and after a silent norm change are judged on different scales with no record.
fix: Add version and sha256 fields to config files, include norms_version and code_version in every output, and require a recorded approval for changes.

title: Score explanation does not state how the IQ was derived or that it is unvalidated
claim: The report's IQ explanation says only 'Driven by lexical sophistication and syntactic complexity' while the actual mapping is a linear VFS to IQ band lookup with a CI derived from the confidence tier, not from validation; the README concedes this but the report body (right-to-explanation) does not.

evidence.excerpt: f"  Driven by lexical sophistication (score {vfs_result['lexical']}) and syntactic complexity (score {vfs_result['syntactic']})."
The 95% CI is mathematically derived from the confidence tier, not from validation against a reference population.

impact_on_screened_person: A person told they scored 'Below Average' cannot learn that the number has no empirical validation.
fix: State in every report that the CI is not empirically validated and list the actual mapping and weights; label output 'unvalidated estimate' when no validation study exists.
